shops.name: Okurindo
aliases: 炭火焼濃厚中華そば 奥倫道
shops.address: GS Heim Shibadaimon, 2-1-18 Shibadaimon, Minato-ku, Tokyo 105-0012
shops.description: The shop name, 炭火焼濃厚中華そば, sets out what it serves: charcoal-grilled, thick chuka soba. The broth is built around that charcoal smoke, deep and roasted, with a richness that you do not expect from a bowl this cheap. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery. Ground floor of GS Heim Shibadaimon, a few minutes from Daimon and Hamamatsucho stations, between Zojoji temple and the bay side. A solid, unpretentious bowl in a neighborhood that does not get the ramen tourist traffic.
shops.note: Coordinates recovered from the plus code MQ43+M5 Minato City (full code 8Q7XMQ43+M5). Everything here comes from the Google listing supplied; hours and prices change, so check before going. Phone +81 3-3438-0188.
shops.coordinateSource: Plus code MQ43+M5 supplied with the Google listing

shops.name: Homemade Ramen Muginae
shops.description: If you are looking for an outstanding ramen experience, I highly recommend Homemade Ramen Muginae. I visited recently, and despite not typically favoring shoyu broths, their version completely won me over with its depth and rich umami flavor. The noodles and toppings were exceptional. The steak in the deluxe toppings was some of the best I have had. Nine consecutive years on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list, and it has ranked as high as second in all of Tokyo. Chef Fukaya Akihiro uses no MSG, no yeast extracts, no chemical seasonings of any kind. The broth is built from Kuroge wagyu, black pork, free-range chicken, and premium dried sardines (iriko). The chashu includes black pork, Hayashi SPF pork, and rare wagyu misuji. The signature side is fish rice: bluefin tuna from the owner's family fish shop, cooked in a claypot with Uonuma rice. Eight to ten counter seats in a quiet residential Shinagawa neighborhood near Omorikaigan station. Reservations open on TableCheck at midnight, one week before the desired date. A limited number of walk-in seats are released each morning via a sign-up board outside around 9:00 a.m. (Read the board. Sign your name. Come back at the assigned time. Do not be late. Trust me, the wait is worth it.)
shops.note: Muginae is the spelling used by the shop; the supplied translated listing calls it Muginawa. Reservations via TableCheck open at midnight one week before. Walk-in registration begins around 9:00 a.m. The shop asks guests to avoid strong fragrances; each guest orders one serving of noodles.

shops.name: Kohaku — Tokyo Honten
aliases: 宍道湖しじみ中華蕎麦 琥珀
shops.description: Five consecutive years Michelin Bib Gourmand. Five counter seats. Reservation only. Chef Iwata Hiroyuki is from Shimane, home of Lake Shinji, and he builds the bowl around its freshwater clams. The broth is clear, golden, no MSG, with roughly eighty clams contributing their natural succinic acid per bowl. Chicken bones round out the base. The result is delicate and powerfully umami at the same time, and it does not taste like any pork- or fish-based Tokyo shop. Straight thin noodles from Suga no Seimen. The shoyu bowl lets you choose thin or hand-kneaded medium-thick. Iwata trained for about five years with the Mendokoro Honda group before opening here in May 2019. Near Zoshiki station on the Keihin Kyuko line, in a residential backstreet of Ota-ku. Quiet, old-school, hard to reach as a tourist. Worth the trip.
shops.note: The Tokyo main store near Zoshiki, not a different Kohaku branch. Reservation-only via TableCheck. Check current business days before booking. Also accessible on foot from JR Kamata station (about 15 minutes).

shops.name: Chuka Soba Shibata
shops.description: Chef Shibata Takashi is a former sound engineer who trained at Menya Musashi and Onmen Shuka Rakuraku in Kichijoji before opening his own shop. His broth uses Aizu jidori, Hinai jidori, Tanba black chicken, and Tsugaru duck, plus kombu and dried seafood. The tare is a proprietary blend of seven to eleven raw soy sauces with duck fat. The noodles are one hundred percent Hokkaido wheat, made in-house since about 2022. You can choose thin straight or hand-kneaded thick wavy. Founded in Sengawa in 2013, relocated to Komae in September 2024, about thirty seconds from the south exit. Komae is a small city in western Tokyo on the Odakyu line, outside the 23 wards. (It is a ramen detour, not a walking tour of central Tokyo. Go for the bowl.)
shops.note: Moved from Sengawa to Komae in September 2024. This is the current address, not the old Wakabacho or Sengawa location. Closed Thursdays and Sundays. Twenty-three seats, but lines after the move are still long.
shops.coordinateSource: Restaurant GeoCoordinates in current Tabelog listing 13300645

shops.name: Shuuichi — Ebisu
shops.address: YAMA Building B1F, 1-9-2 Ebisunishi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
shops.description: A curry ramen shop from Ramen Heads. A personal favorite. Not a shoyu shop. Not a tonkotsu shop. Shuuichi is a curry tsukemen specialist, and that is a different animal. The dipping sauce is a creamy, spice-forward curry that behaves like ramen broth, not like curry udon. Medium-thick curly noodles from Asahusa Kaikaro stand up to the weight of it. You choose your heat level. At lunch, free rice arrives so you can pour the leftover curry over it and eat it like risotto. Open until 5:00 a.m. Tuesday through Saturday. Down a basement stair in the YAMA Building, two minutes from Ebisu station west exit. Ebisu is one of Tokyo's great eating neighborhoods, walkable and dense, and this is the 4 a.m. bowl after you have been everywhere else.
shops.note: Saved as Shuuichi (Ramen). The restaurant is below street level; look for the stairway entrance. Closed Sundays. Operated by Birth Corporation.

shops.name: Usagi
aliases: ラーメン うさぎ 渋谷
shops.address: Argus Shimota Building 1F, 8-13 Shinsencho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
shops.description: A tantanmen specialist a few minutes from Shinsen station, back from the noise of Dogenzaka. Counter seats only, ten of them, cash only. Open weekday lunch only, 11:30 to 14:30 with last order at 14:00, closed Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Reviewers name the tantanmen, the soupless version, and a truffle soy sauce ramen. Budget runs under 1,000 yen at the low end. A small, focused shop that does one thing seriously.
shops.note: Coordinates are the centroid of the Shinsencho district from the Geolonia open address dataset, not a surveyed door position, so the pin is accurate to a block. Phone +81 3-3464-4111. Replaces the closed Emoto pin in this area.

shops.name: Ramenya Shima
shops.description: Ramen-ya Shima in Nishi-Shinjuku delivers an extraordinary ramen experience that is worth every bit of effort to secure a reservation. The rich soy sauce broth has a sharpness and depth that is perfectly complemented by tender, thin noodles, while the toppings, from soft char siu to runny-yolk eggs, add layers of texture and flavor. Both the soy sauce and salt ramen options are outstanding, with the salt version bringing a subtle, savory punch that lingers beautifully. Paired with the grilled char siu rice, this bowl of ramen stands among Japan's best, making each visit a blissful culinary highlight. Chef Hiroshi Morishima trained under the late Minoru Sano at Shinasobaya (the shop that arguably defined modern Tokyo shoyu), then at Kashiwagi, then opened here in June 2020. Six counter seats. The seasonal wakamatsu bowl adds grape pepper (sansho) to a white-shoyu base, and it is the one people chase. Reservations open the day before at 8:00 a.m. on TableCheck and fill in minutes. (If you miss the window, you miss the bowl.)
shops.note: Near Nishi-Shinjuku-Gochome station, but the address is in Shibuya ward. The old same-day sign-up system has ended; cancellations do not guarantee walk-in entry. The dashi contains shrimp.

shops.name: Nagi — Golden Gai
shops.station: Shinjuku-sanchome (Marunouchi / Fukutoshin / Toei Shinjuku) — 3 min walk
shops.description: A restaurant featured in Ramen Heads. Up a steep stair in Shinjuku Golden Gai, the postwar alley of bars too narrow for a car to pass through. Nagi boils over twenty kinds of dried fish for its broth. The result is opaque, intensely oceanic, slicked with fish oil, and not for everyone. (Some people love it. Some people think it tastes like low tide. Both reactions are valid.) Founded by Ikuta Satoshi, open 24 hours, 365 days a year. The thick wavy noodles are house-made. You choose shio or shoyu tare, noodle firmness, oil level, and spice. This is the late-night, post-bar, shime-ramen choice.
shops.note: The Golden Gai Honkan branch. Duplicate saved-list and KML entries are combined here. Cash only. Expect a queue at peak hours even at 3 a.m.

shops.name: Homemade Noodles Honma
shops.station: Komagome (JR Yamanote) — 6 min walk from east exit
shops.style: Chicken paitan and vegetable potage, homemade noodles
shops.description: Honma Eikichi is from Sakata in the Shonai region of Yamagata Prefecture, which ranked first in the General Election for Local Ramen in Japan. He grew up eating ramen and working in ramen shops, spent eleven years at a major chain, and opened his own ten-seat U-shaped cypress counter in May 2019. The menu always has about ten bowls on it, which is unusual and intentional: in Yamagata, ramen is how you welcome people, and variety is the hospitality. The signature is Special Shio (1,300 yen), a chicken paitan built on whole Daisen chickens and their bones, combined with a vegetable potage of Inca no Mezame potatoes from Hokkaido, onions from Awaji Island, and fresh cream. The result is thick, rich, and balanced, more like a Western potage than a standard ramen soup. Noodles are homemade daily from Haruyokoi flour (Hokkaido), laid overnight to remove water, which gives them a brownish tinge and a soft, glutinous texture. No chemical seasonings. Other bowls rotate through the year: umakara (spicy, with mackerel and bonito flakes), shoyu, clam salt, shottsuru, tsukemen, and a limited summer corn ramen made with Dolce Dream corn grown by a farmer in Morioka he personally commissions. Closed Tuesdays.
shops.note: Coordinates approximated from the Honkomagome 5-chome neighborhood centroid (OpenStreetMap). Hours: lunch 11:00 to 15:00 (14:00 some sources), dinner 18:00 to 21:00, Sunday lunch only. Check @jikaseimenhonma on X for current menu and seasonal items.

shops.name: Ramen Kamo to Negi — Ueno Okachimachi
shops.description: The name means duck and leek, and the broth is made from only three things: duck, green onion, and water. No chemical seasonings. Chef Amatsuchi Masayasu simmers domestic aigamo duck low and slow until the soup is clear, light, and deeply flavored. You choose two of three negi preparations: grilled whole leek, white-hair negi, or Kyoto Kujo negi. The duck chashu is confit-style, juicy and tender. Thin straight noodles made with Japanese whole-wheat flour. Open 24 hours. The ticket machine has English. Ueno and Okachimachi are old shitamachi, near the park and the Ameyoko market streets, and there are two ramen shops on this map within a few minutes' walk of each other. (This is the one that proves ramen can be clean, light, and still hit like a freight train.)
shops.note: Original saved pin. A nearby Shinkan (new) branch uses 6-3-5 Ueno; check which branch you want before travelling. Lines can exceed 30 to 50 minutes at peak.

shops.name: Aidaya
shops.address: 101B, Okachimachi Green Heights, 6-1-6 Ueno, Taito-ku, Tokyo
shops.style: Tsukemen · choose two of four dipping sauces
shops.description: A tsukemen specialist where you pick two of four dipping sauces and switch between them in one meal. The four: tonkotsu-gyokai (pork bone and fish, the signature), ebi (a bisque-like shrimp sauce with a tomato-based secret ingredient), garlic shoyu (pork and chicken with soy, mirin, raw garlic), and tantan (sesame paste, chili oil, vinegar). The noodles are house-made, reportedly fifty percent udon flour, thick and chewy. You choose hiyamori (cold, firmer) or kamaage (warm, straight from the pot). The kuroge wagyu sirloin rice bowl is a popular side. Nine counter seats. This is the sixth brand of the Koike Group (Ramen Koike, Chuka Soba Nishino, King Seimen, Tsukemen Kinryu, Koike no Iekei). Not Aidaya 2.
shops.note: The Ueno shop from the supplied listing, not Aidaya 2. Two minutes from JR Okachimachi north exit. Popular at lunch; the line often forms before opening.

shops.name: Kikanbō — Kanda
shops.station: Kanda (JR Yamanote / Chuo / Keihin-Tohoku; Ginza) — 2 min walk
shops.description: It is spicy, and you are gonna wait. One of the best ramen dishes in Tokyo. Come for my Oni level, if you dare. Kikanbo's bowl is kara-shibi miso: spicy (kara) and numbing (shibi, from Japanese sansho). You set your own levels on a five-point scale for each, from none to oni-mashi, which is devil-level and costs extra. The broth is a rich miso blend with pork, chicken, dried fish, and seafood, finished with chili and fragrant sansho oil. Thick, chewy yellow noodles. The interior is black paint, taiko music, and festival-style devil masks, and it adds to the immersive dining experience. (Feel free to challenge my Oni title. We can sit side by side if you live that spicy life.) Opened 2009 by Miura Masakazu. Kanda is old shitamachi Tokyo, north of the Imperial Palace, under the JR tracks between Kanda and Akihabara. Bookshops and curry houses, not skyscrapers. The line is 30 to 60 minutes at peak.
shops.note: Kanda flagship. One pin combines the KML, Favorites and Want to go entries. Start at normal for both chili and sansho before you go higher. International branches exist in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Australia.

shops.name: Tokyo Ramen Street
shops.address: First Avenue Tokyo Station B1F, 1-9-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
shops.description: Not one shop. A curated basement hall of ten ramen restaurants under Tokyo Station, on the Yaesu side outside the ticket gates. As of the 2025 renewal: Rokurinsha (the famous tsukemen shop), Soranairo NIPPON (shoyu and vegan, gluten-free, Michelin-listed), Hirugao (shio specialist), Tokyo Station Ikaruga (tonkotsu-gyokai double soup), and six more covering miso, ie-kei, niboshi, and regional pop-ups. This is the most efficient way to try several top styles in one lunch hour without leaving the station. (Prepare to wait.) Queues at peak. Go off-peak. Check the floor guide for current tenants, because the lineup rotates.
shops.note: A collection of ramen restaurants, not a single shop. Underground on the Yaesu side, outside the ticket gates. Check the official floor guide for current tenants before visiting.
